stories.title: Satellite Images Show Extent of Trump Admin’s Tree-Felling at DC Golf Course, Despite ‘Furious’ Judge’s Order
stories.text: Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published . Satellite imagery obtained by Bellingcat lays bare the extent of tree-felling at a Washington DC golf course that President Trump is reportedly seeking to transform into a championship-level course, despite moves to protect the site by conservationists. The extent and circumstances surrounding the rapid changes prompted a judge to call an emergency hearing earlier this week, banning any further changes until later this month. Reports on Wednesday detailed that 430 trees were cut down at the East Potomac Golf Links which is owned by the Federal government and managed by the National Park Service (NPS) . This is despite a judge’s order issued earlier this year that required court approval to cut down more than 10 trees at the course. U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes was reported to have said that the government’s actions had cost it “all of its credibility with me in this case.” She is also reported to have said she was “ furious ” with the Justice Department for the lack of time afforded the court and plaintiffs before the tree removal was carried out. stories.title: After Ashley Moody Epstein Probe, Donors Linked to Him Poured Money Into her Senate Campaign
stories.text: During her tenure as Florida Attorney General, Sen. Ashley Moody led an investigation into the work-release program that allowed Jeffrey Epstein to engage in sexual encounters while imprisoned for soliciting underage girls for prostitution. After nearly two years of probing, she concluded no wrongdoing. Now Moody, a Republican, is up for reelection in a tight race for a Florida Senate seat against Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon, and she has received $50,000 from individuals connected to Epstein. Douglas Band, a former Bill Clinton staffer who communicated with Ghislaine Maxwell to schedule meetings between the former president and Jeffrey Epstein, donated $14,000 to Moody’s victory fund on April 15. Blackstone CEO Stephen Schwarzman and John Catsimatidis, two billionaires who appeared respectively in call logs and address books in the Epstein files, donated the next most to Moody’s fund at $12,000 and $10,000 a pop. stories.text: Metallica frontman James Hetfield gave a concert at the Las Vegas Sphere over the weekend, and kicked off with a few words about his band’s “agenda”: Thanks for coming to celebrate with us. And I just gotta say: Metallica is not here, like some other entertainers, to influence you with their bullshit. We are here to forget about all the outside shit. Metallica’s agenda is love, energy, and heavy music, baby! On cue, every activist on the planet lined up to denounce the band. My own former podcast cohost Katie Halper called Hetfield a “ loser and a coward ” and had former Pink Floyd lead Roger Waters on to deploy the obligatory talking points that not only is Hetfield spineless, but Metallica sucks and always has (“never heard anything so appallingly out of tune in my life… can’t play a note”). Waters added: “I’m apolitical” is not an option. Nobody can step away from this. You are being killed. Gaza is just the first bit. They’ll get to you. Don’t you worry. They’ll either enslave you or murder you. Because that’s that’s their ethos. This goes back, you know, 500 years, to the beginning of European white settler colonialism. Since Trump cast doubt on the livestream, reports have claimed he had a change of heart upon realizing Hasan is wheelchair-bound. stories.title: Pulling Out Teeth Just to Live: How Israel Has Devastated Dental Care in Gaza
stories.text: DEIR AL-BALAH, Gaza Strip—At midnight, inside a tent in Deir al-Balah, Nour Abo Shamala put her head against the pillow with a plastic cup of salt water beside her. Sleep didn’t come. A bolt of pain ran from her front tooth to the top of her skull and across her head. The only sounds in the night were the wind outside and her groans. She felt around for the plastic cup in the darkness and rinsed her mouth with the water. It brought no relief to the ache in her upper jaw. She soaked a rag in cold water, pressed it against her mouth, and waited for dawn. Abo Shamala, 22, has lived with this chronic pain since February. She graduated university with a teaching degree just before the genocide began in October 2023, and has never had the chance to work. The family lives on aid. They were displaced from their home in Jabaliya more than five times before reaching Deir al-Balah in May 2024. This past May, three months after the pain in her tooth first began, she went to one of the few dentists still working in the area.
